references.text: For the first time, Pilate declares that he finds no guilt in Jesus ([ref:Luk 23:4|Luke 23:4]). In verse 22, he repeats this for the third time, emphasizing Jesus' innocence.

Pilate's second declaration of Jesus' innocence, where he also mentions that he will punish him and then release him ([ref:Luk 23:14-16|Luke 23:14-16]). Verse 22 almost word-for-word repeats the same conclusion: "I have found no reason in him to deserve death; therefore I will punish him and set him free."
John also tells that Pilate declared he found no guilt in Jesus ([ref:Joh 18:38|John 18:38]). This is a parallel to Pilate's repeated declarations of innocence in Luke.
Also in [ref:Joh 19:4-6|John 19:4-6], Pilate repeatedly declares that he finds no guilt in Jesus, paralleling Luke's triple declaration of innocence.
In [ref:Matt 27:23|Matthew 27:23], Pilate asks the crowd "What evil has he done?" – exactly the same question Pilate asks in Luke 23:22 (Τί γὰρ κακὸν ἐποίησεν οὗτος;).
In [ref:Mark 15:14|Mark 15:14], Pilate asks the same question: "What evil has he done?" This is a direct parallel to Pilate's words in Luke 23:22.

Peter confirms that Christ had committed no sin ([ref:1 Pet 2:22|1 Peter 2:22]). Pilate's declaration that he found nothing deserving of death in Jesus points to the same truth about Jesus' sinlessness.

Isaiah prophesies about the Lord's suffering servant that "he had done no wrong" ([ref:Jes 53:9|Isaiah 53:9]). Pilate's declaration that he found nothing wrong in Jesus fulfills this prophecy of the innocent who suffers.
In [ref:Apg 13:28|Acts 13:28], Paul says they found no reason for a death sentence, yet still asked Pilate to have him executed – a direct reference to the events described in Luke 23:22.
Paul writes that Christ "knew nothing of sin" ([ref:2 Kor 5:21|2 Corinthians 5:21]). Pilate's testimony that he found nothing deserving of death in Jesus theologically confirms Christ's sinlessness.
